About Sodexo

Founded in Marseille in 1966 by Pierre Bellon, Sodexo is the leader in Food and Services, shaping better everyday experiences at every moment in life: work, heal, learn and play. The Group stands out for its independence, its founding family shareholding and its responsible business model. With its services, Sodexo meets all the challenges of everyday life with a dual goal: to improve the quality of life of our employees and those we serve, and contribute to the economic, social and environmental progress in the communities where we operate. For Sodexo, growth and social commitment go hand in hand. Our purpose is to create a better everyday for everyone to build a better life for all. Sodexo is included in the CAC Next 20, CAC SBT 1.5, FTSE 4 Good and DJSI indices.

data.title: Credit Bureau, Fair Isaac Shares Retreat as FHFA Chief Pulte Slams Industry
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Shares of major credit bureaus and Fair Isaac fell after a top federal housing regulator criticized their prices and the reliance on FICO scores in mortgage lending.

Shares of Fair Isaac, the company behind the FICO score, were down 18% to $922.67 in Friday morning trading. Equifax's stock was off 7.9% at $174.26, TransUnion was down 8% at $78.09, and shares in Experian retreated 4.8% to $37.91 in over-the-counter trading.

Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte took to X on Thursday night to accuse Fair Isaac of operating a monopoly over credit scores. He said he was directing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to approve all lenders using the rival VantageScore model.

The agency had previously greenlit the use of VantageScore 4.0 last summer, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Pulte also accused the three credit bureaus--Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion--of "overcharging Americans for far too long" and stringing along regulators.

"We are seriously considering bi-merge, and stronger solutions (SAFER and SOUNDER)," Pulte wrote in one post. "We will not allow companies to take advantage of American consumers."

The companies named by Pulte did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

"We have asked the CEOs of the Credit Bureaus for solutions but they seem more intent on "happy talk", tapping us along with meetings, and operating as "cartel-like", which is not in the best interest of American homeowners," Pulte said in another post. "Time for a change."

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com

data.title: 5N Plus' U.S. Award Unlocks Defense Long Runway — Market Talk
data.description: 5N Plus is positioned to become only qualified domestic U.S. supplier of gallium arsenide electro-optical components. Desjardin analyst Frederic Tremblay notes the specialty materials company was selected by the U.S. Department of War to receive $7.3 million to establish domestic production of gallium arsenide components for defense applications at its Utah facility. Currently, U.S. defense contractors rely on foreign suppliers. Tremblay says that this could also open the door to future production of gallium arsenide components and other advanced semiconductor materials for other defense and space applications. "This expands VNP's long-term optionality by broadening its addressable market and strengthening its positioning within critical western supply chains," he says. Shares are up 6.5% to C$26.55. (adriano.marchese@wsj.com)

data.title: Wheat continues slide with Ukraine war negotiations in focus
data.description:
By Heather Schlitz

Chicago wheat futures slid on Friday, continuing a pullback from a 3-1/2-year high earlier in the week, with traders watching to see if diplomatic efforts to end Russia's war with Ukraine would ease disruption to crucial Black Sea grain shipments.

Corn and soybeans chopped up and down in positioning ahead of the long weekend and next week's U.S. Department of Agriculture report.

The most-active wheat contract on the Chicago Board of Trade was down 12-1/2 cents to $7.42 a bushel as of 10:10 a.m. CT (1510 GMT).

On Thursday, the benchmark slid following comments by Russian President Vladimir Putin that a peace agreement to end the war in Ukraine remained possible. Putin's remarks triggered profit-taking after Wednesday's peak of $7.95.

"Any talk of peace talks is going to pressure the market," said Ed Duggan, a broker with Top Third Ag Marketing. "Wheat is (in the Black Sea region), but it just can't leave — that's the problem."

REPORTS OF U.S. ENVOYS VISITING RUSSIA, UKRAINE

The Kremlin said on Friday that the possibility of a Ukraine peace settlement remained, but declined to confirm reports that U.S. envoys were expected to visit Russia and Ukraine over the weekend for peace negotiations.

Russian state news agency TASS and U.S. news outlet Axios separately reported that Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner would visit Moscow and Kyiv in the next two days. However, plans for the U.S. envoys to visit Russia and Ukraine this weekend have yet to be finalised because of U.S. security concerns, a source familiar with the situation said.

Tit-for-tat attacks by Russia and Ukraine on each other's ports and shipping have brought the countries' Black Sea exports to a near halt. The squeeze led Asian wheat importers to buy at least half a million metric tons of Australian and Argentine wheat in recent deals, trade sources said this week.

CBOT soybeans edged 1-1/4 cents lower to $13.15 a bushel while CBOT corn fell 1 cent to $5.40 a bushel.

Soybeans have been supported by Chinese purchases of U.S. soybeans and concerns over hot, dry weather in key U.S. growing areas. Expectations for poor yields in the U.S. Corn Belt have kept a floor on corn futures.

The USDA said on Thursday exporters sold 192,000 tons of soybeans to China for delivery in the 2026/27 marketing year.

data.title: Mobile Connectivity Expert GlocalMe Showcases All-Around, Always-On Connectivity at IFA 2026
data.description:
BERLIN, Sept. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GlocalMe, a leading global mobile connectivity brand under the Nasdaq-listed technology solution provider uCloudlink Group Inc. (), showcases its latest lineup of consumer-grade internet solutions at IFA 2026, Europe's largest technology trade show. The brand brings a range of lifestyle gadgets for travelers seeking uninterrupted internet access to support their business and emergency needs.

GlocalMe believes connectivity is the foundation on which AI is built. As the AI wave reshapes how people work and travel, it is connectivity and data flow that will determine how far, how fast, and how intelligently this new era can move.

MeowGo Hotspots: Reliable Communications Even in Remote Areas

At the center of GlocalMe's IFA portfolio is the MeowGo G50 Max, an advanced 5G satellite mobile Wi-Fi hotspot that unifies 5G cellular speed, satellite resilience, and intelligent Wi-Fi management in a single device. Equipped with a Qualcomm QCM4490 chip, it is the first product on the market to pair an AI assistant with a 5G hotspot that keeps working even when base station infrastructure is down — as much an emergency lifeline as a travel companion.

Designed for a broad range of real-world scenarios, the G50 Max doubles as a backup communication tool when it is needed most: through its partnership with Skylo's satellite network, it lets users send SMS messages in 38 destinations even when regular signals go dark during natural disasters or power outages. Unlike other mobile Wi-Fi hotspots on the market, it's also a fully-fledged AI travel assistant, handling translation, exchange-rate conversion, route planning, and more to smooth the whole trip. Backed by uCloudlink's underlying technology and partnerships with 390+ carriers worldwide, the device connects users to internet service in over 200 countries and regions.

Pack Less, Experience More On The Go

Beyond Wi-Fi hotspots, GlocalMe offers a range of multi-in-one lifestyle devices that handle charging, connectivity, and locating all at once—freeing up space in a traveler's backpack. The Life Series and other offerings include the RoamPlug universal travel adapter, the UniCord family of charging cables, the eSIM Trio which brings eSIM connectivity to legacy phones, and a lineup of Wi-Fi hotspot + power bank combos. Each is built around the same principle: global connectivity should live inside the everyday tools travelers already carry, not add another item to pack.

These devices draw on CloudSIM technology to tap directly into the strongest available local signal, and are all managed through a single GlocalMe app.

Powered by the patented HyperConn™ and CloudSIM technologies, GlocalMe products let users connect to fast internet service worldwide without the need for costly roaming. The brand was born to solve pressing needs for frequent travelers and emergency responders who require continuous connectivity across a wide range of complex scenarios.

"As travel and remote work become borderless, we believe connectivity should be too. The world is going through a lot of unexpected events, which have pushed us to build solutions people can truly count on. Our IFA 2026 lineup is built to keep people online in the moments that matter most, wherever they are," said Jeff Chen, CEO and Founder of uCloudlink.

IFA attendees are welcome to visit the booth at Hall 3.2, 143, Messe Berlin, to experience the latest launches in person.

About GlocalMe

GlocalMe is a mobile connectivity brand powered by uCloudlink Group Inc., an industry pioneer in mobile data traffic sharing marketplace and a pioneer of the sharing economy business model in the telecommunications industry.

uCloudlink was listed on the NASDAQ in 2020. The company has redefined the mobile data connectivity experience by enabling users to access data traffic shared by network operators, without requiring a physical SIM card.

SOURCE uCloudlink Group Inc.
